judgements.justification: A had u2eX (9, 7 h) and nnEq (8, 10 h), who checked the proofs and found real slips; no B reviewer rated above 7, and fudr's 7 is a light review that never posted again.
No reviewer in either committee said it read only part of the paper.
B read the paper as an approximation method rather than an explanation (R16), but no reviewer came from a different theoretical tradition or contested the premise.
A's two-sentence meta-review praised the contributions and asked for citations, but stage 1 notes nothing in it explains a spotlight rather than a poster.
B's Xcrv knew the i.i.d.-sampling rates (Fournier and Guillin) and checked the result against them; A's reviewers checked proofs and never asked what the result buys over that baseline.
A's AC overstated the reviewers' view of the experiments in the upward direction; B's AC omitted fudr's 7 but did not misstate any reviewer's final position.
No reviewer or AC raised a narrow-audience or wrong-venue concern.
T7tc misread eq. (15) and rated 6, but A's AC did not argue against that score and A placed the paper in spotlight.
The tightness reply that raised gM3z pointed to Appendix E of the submission; no new experiments or analyses were posted to one forum only.
Neither committee had a lone high-confidence expert outweighed by lower-confidence reviews; B's two confidence-4 reviewers rated 6 and 5.
Xcrv's unanswered follow-up on the uncited gradient-flow claim came with no score change, and no record shows it came after the response period closed.
Stage 1 attributes the rating gap to different weighting of the same gaps, not to one committee scoring similar verbal assessments higher.
Both committees noted the unfulfilled regression framing; neither held the paper to a lower tier because the headline claim was overstated.
No committee's reviewers converged on marginal-accept scores out of inability to check the core; B's ratings split 6/7/5/5 on stated practical concerns.
